sectors.note:
**TL;DR:** Defensive and commodity sectors are driving the market as Healthcare and Basic Materials surge, while Technology and Financials show early signs of fading momentum.

Defensive and commodity-linked sectors are currently driving market strength. Energy remains the top-ranked sector (rank 1, momentum 0.77), but Basic Materials (momentum 0.82) and Healthcare (momentum 0.80) are the primary engines of positive rotation, climbing two and three spots respectively over the last five sessions to secure "all-green" status across all timeframes.

Conversely, growth and cyclical sectors are losing their footing. Technology has slipped one spot to rank 3 despite holding a momentum score of 0.62, while Financials dropped two spots to rank 8 (momentum 0.52). Utilities remains the market's primary laggard, anchored by a momentum score of just 0.08.

## Strength
* **Broad Market Breadth:** 4 out of 11 sectors maintain "all-green" status, showing positive performance across weekly, monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, and YTD horizons.
* **Commodity & Defensive Leaders:** Basic Materials leads the momentum scoreboard at 0.817 (rank 2), closely followed by Healthcare at 0.800 (rank 4) and Energy at 0.767 (rank 1).
* **All-Green Financials:** Financials (momentum 0.517, rank 8) remains in the all-green camp despite experiencing recent ranking pressure.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Healthcare Surging:** Healthcare is the week's biggest gainer, jumping 3 spots to rank 4 with a strong momentum score of 0.80.
* **Basic Materials Climbing:** Basic Materials advanced 2 spots to rank 2, cementing its position as the top momentum leader (0.82).
* **Financials & Industrials Slipping:** Financials and Industrials are the week's biggest losers, both dropping 2 spots to rank 8 (momentum 0.52) and rank 5 (momentum 0.30) respectively.
* **Deep Laggards:** Utilities remains anchored at the bottom of the momentum rankings at 0.083 (rank 9), alongside Consumer Cyclicals at 0.383 (rank 11).

## Divergences
* **Technology Fading:** Technology shows early warning signs of fading, slipping 1 spot to rank 3 over the last 5 days despite holding a relatively strong momentum score of 0.62.
* **Fragile Materials Strength:** Despite leading overall momentum (0.817), Basic Materials shows low internal agreement of 0.38, signaling its "all-green" status may be unstable.
* **Unstable Financials:** Financials (momentum 0.52) is also flagged as a fragile "all-green" sector with a low agreement score of 0.44, compounded by its 2-spot rank drop.

industries.note:
**TL;DR:** A powerful bid in metals and mining (Copper, Coking Coal, Gold) and persistent strength in employment services are driving the market, while Aerospace & Defense and Renewable Utilities suffer sharp weekly pullbacks.

Market breadth remains concentrated, with only 26 of 143 industry groups maintaining "all-green" status across all timeframes. Copper (0.93 momentum) and Staffing & Employment Services (0.88 momentum) continue to lead the broader market. We are seeing a major rotation into commodities, as Gold surged 38 spots to rank 32 and Coking Coal climbed 36 spots to rank 63, joining the ranks of sustained momentum leaders.

Conversely, industrial and green energy sectors are fading rapidly. Aerospace & Defense plummeted 37 spots to rank 110, while Renewable Utilities dropped 36 spots to rank 103. Additionally, early warning signs are emerging in financial and tech software groups, where ranks are slipping despite still-elevated momentum scores.

## Strength
* **All-Green Breadth:** Only 18% of the market (26 of 143 groups) is positive across all weekly, monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, and YTD horizons, led by Copper (0.93 momentum) and Staffing & Employment Services (0.88 momentum).
* **Sustained Leadership:** Groups exhibiting persistent top-tier performance over 1-, 3-, and 6-month windows include Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (0.88 momentum), Biotechnology (0.87 momentum), Diagnostics & Research (0.83 momentum), and Health Information Services (0.81 momentum).

## Movers & Momentum
* **Top Gainers:** Precious metals and resources experienced a sharp weekly demand shock, led by Gold (+38 spots to rank 32, 0.82 momentum), Coking Coal (+36 spots to rank 63, 0.86 momentum), and Other Precious Metals & Mining (+31 spots to rank 79, 0.70 momentum).
* **Top Losers:** Heavy industrials and transport fell out of favor, with Aerospace & Defense dropping 37 spots to rank 110 (0.28 momentum), Renewable Utilities falling 36 spots to rank 103 (0.20 momentum), and Aluminum losing 34 spots to rank 83 (0.36 momentum).
* **Momentum Extremes:** Copper (0.933) and Staffing & Employment Services (0.885) lead the absolute momentum rankings, while Independent Power Producers (0.060) and Advertising Agencies (0.072) remain anchored at the bottom.

## Divergences
* **Fading Leaders:** Early-warning weakness is showing up in Capital Markets (0.65 momentum, -6 spots), Software - Infrastructure (0.63 momentum, -6 spots), and Diversified Banks (0.64 momentum, -4 spots), which are losing rank despite solid momentum.
* **Emerging Defensive Value:** Low-momentum, defensive value groups are quietly climbing the ranks, led by Household & Personal Products (+16 spots, 0.47 momentum), Tobacco (+12 spots, 0.43 momentum), and Regulated Water Utilities (+9 spots, 0.46 momentum).
